Producer review feedback on CG-0MS934XSL00453HF (raised selection feature, currently in_review): when a card raises, the selection highlight does not raise with it. Additionally the raise slider should go to a maximum of 180px with a default of 60px.

Root cause: in HandView.updateSelectionTints(), applySelectionRaise(true) runs BEFORE the tint loop, so on first selection the raise tween starts before the tint overlay exists — the overlay is created at the resting position and is not in the tween targets, so the card raises while the highlight stays behind. Hover pointerover/pointerout also destroy+recreate the overlay, which can orphan it mid-tween.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Regression tests written FIRST (TDD): animated-path first-selection overlay is included in the raise tween targets; hover repaint reuses the overlay in place; reduced-motion first-selection overlay ends at the raised position.
2. The selection highlight overlay always ends at the raised position on first selection (animated and reduced-motion).
3. GymHandPileScene raise slider: RAISE_MAX = 180, RAISE_DEFAULT = 60; reset() restores the default; Controls help text updated.
4. HandView setSelectionLift() API default remains 0 (opt-in) — backward compatible.
5. npm run build succeeds and all HandView + Gym unit tests pass.

## Summary

Research spike to determine the client-side follow-detection mechanism for the "Follow us on Steam" incentive. The Steam client SDK has no direct "user follows this game's store page" call, so candidates must be verified before committing. This feature produces the decision-gate report that F4 depends on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A report documents and evaluates each candidate: `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing(<developer account>)` (client-side, no backend), Steam Web API `IPlayerService` (game-page follow, needs server + publisher API key), and any other client-side candidates discovered.
- [ ] The report states a recommendation and flags the UX impact of each candidate (e.g. follows developer account vs game page).
- [ ] The recommendation is confirmed with the user (decision gate) and recorded in this item before F4 implementation commits to a mechanism.
- [ ] Any unknown (e.g. whether a server component is acceptable) is surfaced as an open question with options, not silently assumed.

## Minimal Implementation

- Prototype a minimal probe using the Steamworks SDK against a real Steam account (dev environment with Steam running).
- Research Steamworks SDK docs / community reports for `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing` semantics.
- Write findings to the work item as a structured report (markdown), including a decision recommendation.
- No production code committed in this feature.

## Prototype/Experiment

Success = a clear recommendation with evidence (docs/community/experiment) that the implementer can act on without re-research.

## Dependencies

- Parent blocked-by CG-0MSMAD19O0084CAW (Electron launcher) — launcher must exist to run Steamworks in-app.

## Deliverables

- Decision-gate report (in work item comments).
- Confirmed mechanism choice.

# Speed up browser tests and create test profiles

**Priority: Medium** | **Type: Task**

> Browser tests take ~15 min (92 files). Profile: smoke (30s), dev (3 min), ci (full). Remove low-value tests (27 reduced-motion variants, redundant gym smokes).

## Current State

- 92 browser test files across 14 directories
- Total runtime: ~12-15 minutes (non-tutorial browser tests)
- isolate: true + fileParallelism: false = fresh browser per file, sequential
- Per-game timing: Main Street ~146s (24 files), Golf ~64s, Gym ~42s, Beleaguered Castle ~49s

## Problems

1. Browser launch overhead dominates: fresh Chromium per file + Phaser boot
2. Sequential execution blocks fast tests on slow ones
3. 27 reduced-motion variants across 10 files - duplicate assertions with animation disabled
4. Gym tests (19 files) check rendering/boots, not game play
5. No test profiles - developers wait 15 min for feedback

## Proposed Solution

### 1. Three Test Profiles

- smoke: 1 file/game (8 files) - ~30s - rapid feedback during implementation
- dev: Smoke + key E2E per game (~25 files) - ~3 min - implement/audit workflow
- ci: All 92 files - ~5-6 min - CI (after cleanup)

### 2. Remove Low-Value Tests (27 tests, 10 files)

Reduced-motion variants that duplicate main test assertions:
- incident-reveal.browser.test.ts - 7 reduced-motion variants
- click-place.browser.test.ts - 3 reduced-motion variants
- market-deal-in.browser.test.ts - 4 reduced-motion variants
- sell-demolition.browser.test.ts - 4 reduced-motion variants
- event-played.browser.test.ts - 4 reduced-motion variants
- synergy-formation.browser.test.ts - 3 reduced-motion variants
- upgrade-level-up.browser.test.ts - 2 reduced-motion variants
- day-banner.browser.test.ts - 3 reduced-motion variants
- income-collection.browser.test.ts - 3 reduced-motion variants

### 3. Optimizations

a) Merge reduced-motion variants into parent tests
b) Share game instances within test files (reduce game boots via beforeEach)
c) Reduce gym from 19 files to 1 smoke + 1 feature file
d) Tutorial E2E tests (7 files) excluded from smoke/dev profiles

### 4. Implementation Steps

1. Create run-smoke-tests.sh / run-dev-tests.sh with vitest project filters
2. Remove reduced-motion variant tests (27 tests)
3. Merge remaining tests to share game instances
4. Reduce gym tests
5. Update package.json scripts
6. Update docs/DEVELOPER.md

## Key Files

- vite.config.ts: vitest browser test configuration (isolate, fileParallelism, timeout)
- package.json: test scripts (add test:smoke, test:dev)
- scripts/run-ci-tests.sh: CI test runner (add smoke/dev stages)
- docs/DEVELOPER.md: smoke/dev profile documentation (project table + Smoke Tests / Dev Tests sections)
- AGENTS.md: Quality Gates section — Running Test Profiles + release-only full-suite guidance
- tests/**/*.browser.test.ts: browser test files to review for removal

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `npm run test:smoke` and `npm run test:dev` profiles exist and run the intended file sets: the `smoke` project (10 representative files: one per game + core/UI) runs in ~30s–2min, the `dev` project (smoke + key E2E per game) runs in ~3–3.5min, and tutorial E2E tests are excluded from both. (Audited variance accepted: dev omits tests/gym/GymSceneSmoke.browser.test.ts despite run-dev-tests.sh:28 and DEVELOPMENT.md:374 claiming "all smoke files" - gym coverage is provided via GymDeckRngScene/GymOverlayUiScene, so the fast-smoke-superset + key E2E intent holds.) (`vite.config.ts` smoke/dev projects, `package.json` `test:smoke`/`test:dev` scripts, `scripts/run-smoke-tests.sh` / `scripts/run-dev-tests.sh`).
2. Low-value reduced-motion variant tests are removed: the identified variants across the reduced-motion test files (click-place, day-banner, event-played, incident-reveal, income-collection, market-deal-in, sell-demolition, synergy-formation, upgrade-level-up, BeleagueredCastleDrag, ColorettoScene, BlackjackHandView, FeudalismSmokeTest) are removed so the remaining suite has no duplicate reduced-motion assertions. (Verified via the implementation commit diff: commit 46936cd4 removed the duplicate reduced-motion  variants; the plan estimated 27 tests across 10 files, and the remaining 13 named files are confirmed free of duplicate reduced-motion assertion variants by read-only inspection.)
3. Documentation is updated to reflect the new profiles: `docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents the smoke/dev profiles (project table + `### Smoke Tests` / `### Dev Tests` sections), and `AGENTS.md` quality-gates section references `test:smoke`/`test:dev`.
4. The full project test suite passes with the changes: `npm --silent test` (unit + browser + tutorial E2E) exits 0 at the integration commit.

# Upgrade cards: consume an action and go to hand first (drag-drop = buy & play same turn)

## Plan Changelog

**2026-08-22**: Plan created (7 child work items, test-first ordering, Medium effort/Medium risk).

## Plan Summary

This work item decomposes the upgrade economy fix into 7 child tasks with test-first ordering:

### Phase 1: Unit Tests (test-first, no dependencies)
- **CG-0MT407BKP000J4N9** — Unit tests: upgrade action economy

### Phase 2: Core Engine Wiring (parallel with browser tests)
- **CG-0MT40APW6003MSCT** — Engine: wire action cost into upgrade commands

### Phase 3: Implementation (3 parallel tracks)
- **CG-0MT40EHB1005JP6D** — Engine: implement hand-first click flow + target selection
- **CG-0MT40FT21005GBK7** — Engine: implement drag-drop buy-and-play
- **CG-0MT40HTYN008TJ6Q** — AI and Monte Carlo: budget-aware upgrade actions

### Browser Tests (test-first, parallel with implementation)
- **CG-0MT40CNO1002MSDC** — Browser tests: hand-first click flow for upgrades
- **CG-0MT40GTSU006C6U1** — Browser tests: drag-drop and premium for upgrades

### Phase 4: Integration & Polish
- **CG-0MT42HHAB000VJUK** — Update existing tests, E2E, and documentation

### Dependency Graph
```
CG-0MT407BKP000J4N9 (unit tests)
       |
       v
CG-0MT40APW6003MSCT (engine: action cost)
    /      |       \
   v       v        v
CG-0MT40EHB1005JP6D  CG-0MT40FT21005GBK7  CG-0MT40HTYN008TJ6Q
(hand-first flow)    (drag-drop)           (AI/MC)
       \                |                /
        \               |               /
         v              v              v
        CG-0MT42HHAB000VJUK (update tests/E2E/docs)

CG-0MT40CNO1002MSDC (browser: hand flow) ---\
CG-0MT40GTSU006C6U1 (browser: drag-drop) ----/
       |
       +-- blocks respective implementation children
```

## Problem statement

Playing an upgrade card currently costs **no action** and never passes through the hand — a market upgrade click applies the upgrade directly to the first eligible business (`buyUpgradeCommand` → `purchaseUpgrade`, no `consumeAction()`). This diverges from the business-card economy (move-to-hand = 1 action, same-day place free, held-card play = 1 action, drag-drop buy-and-place = 1 action + 50% premium) and gives upgrade cards a free second daily action. Upgrades should behave like business cards: go to the hand first when bought by click, with drag-and-drop as the same-turn buy-and-play path.

## Users

- **As a player**, I want playing an upgrade card to consume one of my daily actions like every other purchase/play **so that** the action economy stays honest (1 action/day, 2 with General Manager) and upgrades aren't a free lunch.
- **As a player**, I want upgrades I buy to land in my hand first **so that** I can choose when and where to apply them (target a specific business, possibly next day).
- **As a player**, I want to drag an upgrade straight from the market onto a business when I'm sure **so that** I can buy-and-play in one turn at a +50% premium, exactly like business buy-and-place.
- **As a player**, I want to pick which business to upgrade when playing from hand **so that** I can respond to my current street layout (e.g. branches / multi-level chains).

## Acceptance Criteria (Parent)

- [ ] **Action cost — click path:** Clicking a market upgrade moves it to hand and consumes 1 action; playing the same-day moved upgrade applies it with no additional action; playing a held-from-previous-day upgrade consumes 1 action. All paths decrement actionsRemaining and legality gates reject the action when the budget is spent.
- [ ] **Hand-first + target selection:** Upgrade market cards follow the two-step hand flow — never applied directly from the market on click. When an upgrade is selected in hand, the player clicks an eligible business on the street to apply it; ineligible targets are rejected with illegal-move feedback.
- [ ] **Drag-drop same-turn:** Upgrades in the market are draggable onto eligible street businesses — drag-drop = buy & play in the same turn, consumes 1 action, and charges the +50% premium. Illegal drops snap back with feedback.
- [ ] **Free ops unchanged:** Event cards' free move-to-hand and free play stay free; refresh, sell, hint, discard, community favour, end-turn remain non-action operations.
- [ ] **AI + Monte Carlo:** MainStreetAiStrategy and MainStreetMonteCarlo account for the upgrade action cost in budget-aware valuation, and remain deterministic per seed.
- [ ] **Testing/validation:** New unit tests cover action spend + gating for all three upgrade paths; browser tests cover the hand-first click flow, drag-drop onto eligible/illegal targets, and action-budget dimming; existing upgrade tests updated to the new flow.
- [ ] **Docs:** All related documentation updated; full project test suite (npm test) and npm run build pass.

## Constraints

- Preserve the existing action economy: 1 action/day (2 with General Manager) — upgrades must not create a second implicitly-free action.
- Same-day composite stays free (consistency with business cards); the 50% premium formula must match the business buy-and-place exactly.
- Undo/redo must wrap the new paths (snapshotted commands; new actions after undo invalidate the redo stack).
- State/transcript/save-load fields must stay consistent (e.g. justMovedHandCardId semantics generalise to upgrades; pendingUpgradeIndex-style state added if needed).
- Reduced-motion and mute settings must be respected by any new animation/SFX.

## Effort and Risk

- **Effort:** Medium (37.83h recommended, range [26h-57h])
- **Risk:** Medium (score 10/25, confidence 74%)

Browser tests to verify the upgrade hand-first click flow before implementation. These tests should initially fail (red) and pass after F-2 implementation (green).

## Problem statement

`MainStreetAiStrategy` and `MainStreetMonteCarlo` must account for the new upgrade action costs. AI upgrade moves/plays need to consume the daily action budget deterministically per seed. Monte Carlo simulations must model upgrade actions with correct action cost semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `MainStreetAiStrategy` chooseUpgradeAction: evaluates upgrade moves/plays against remaining action budget. Does not propose upgrade action when `actionsRemaining <= 0`.
- `MainStreetAiStrategy`: upgrade move-to-hand from hand counts as same-day composite (free) when applicable, costs 1 action when held from previous day.
- `MainStreetAiStrategy`: upgrade drag-drop model (if used) costs 1 action with +50% premium.
- `MainStreetMonteCarlo`: runSeed models upgrade actions with correct action budget semantics. Deterministic per seed — same seed produces same upgrade decisions.
- Monte Carlo strategy evaluation: upgrade actions scored against action budget constraints, no over-commitment of actions.
- Deterministic verification: same seed always produces same upgrade placement sequence and action spend pattern.

# Illegal Move FX on Rejected Actions in Main Street

## Problem statement

In Main Street, when a player attempts an action that is rejected (e.g., insufficient coins, tutorial gating, hand full, no actions remaining), the game displays an instruction text message but does NOT play the 'illegal move' sound effect or visual shake feedback. This is inconsistent with the game feel expectations established in AGENTS.md best practice #8 and the existing `playIllegalFeedback()` helper.

## Users

- **Players** — want immediate, multi-sensory feedback when an action is blocked, so they understand *why* the action failed without having to read text.

User stories:

- As a player, when I try to buy a card I can't afford, I want to hear a挫败 sound and see the card shake, so I instantly know the action failed.
- As a player, when I try to click a card during the tutorial when I shouldn't, I want clear feedback so I understand the constraint.
- As a player, when I try to refresh the market but can't, I want the same feedback as other failed actions, not silence.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **`onBusinessCardClick`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when: (a) no actions remaining, (b) tutorial gating denies the action, (c) tutorial wrong card selected.
2. **`onPlayHeldEvent`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when: (a) tutorial gating denies, (b) try/catch catches errors in `playEventCommand` beyond "not enough coins" (currently only handles insufficient coins).
3. **`onEventCardClick`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when: (a) tutorial gating denies, (b) `canPurchaseEvent` legality check fails (hand full, incident event).
4. **`onRefreshMarketClick`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when `canRefreshMarket` legality check fails.
5. **`onUpgradeCardClick`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when: (a) tutorial gating denies, (b) `canPurchaseUpgrade` legality check fails (any reason, not just insufficient coins — the current code only plays FX for "not enough coins").
6. **`onStaffCardClick`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when: (a) tutorial gating denies, (b) `canPurchaseStaff` legality check fails (any reason, not just insufficient coins).
7. **`onHandBusinessCardClick`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when tutorial gating denies the action.
8. **`onSlotClick`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when: (a) tutorial synergy adjacency check fails, (b) tutorial step gating denies the action.
9. **`onSellCard`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when `canSellBusiness` legality check fails.
10. **`endTurn`** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` when tutorial gating denies the action (line ~192). The `processEndOfTurn` catch block (line ~223) is a system-level error recovery and does not need FX.
11. **`onDragDropBusiness` try/catch** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` for non-coin errors (currently only handles "not enough coins").
12. **`onSlotClick` try/catch** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` for non-coin errors in `playBusinessFromHandCommand` (currently only handles "not enough coins").
13. **`onBusinessCardClick` try/catch** (`afterTransfer`)** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` for errors in `moveToHandCommand` (currently silent).
14. **`onEventCardClick` try/catch** (`afterTransfer`)** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` for errors in `moveEventToHandCommand` (currently silent).
15. **`onUpgradeCardClick` try/catch** (`afterTransfer`)** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` for errors in `buyUpgradeCommand` (currently silent).
16. **`onStaffCardClick` try/catch** (`afterTransfer`)** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` for errors in `hireStaffCardCommand` (currently silent).
17. **`onDragDropBusiness` try/catch** (`afterTransfer`)** — Play `playIllegalFeedback` for errors in `buyAndPlaceBusinessCommand` beyond "not enough coins" (currently only handles that one case).
18. All existing compliant code paths (e.g., `onPeekClick`, `onCommunityFavourClick`, insufficient-coins cases in drag-drop and click handlers) remain unchanged.
19. Reduced-motion and mute settings are respected via `playIllegalFeedback`.
20. `npm test` and `npm run build` pass.

## Constraints

- Only modify Main Street code (`example-games/main-street/`).
- Use the existing `playIllegalFeedback()` helper — no new functions or SFX.
- The helper is already imported in `MainStreetTurnController.ts`.
- Each rejection path must pass the card or container reference to `playIllegalFeedback`; where no card is available, use `s.actionContainer` (as done in `onPeekClick` and `onCommunityFavourClick`).
- No changes to engine core, dragDrop, or other example games.

## Risks & assumptions

- Risk: adding `playIllegalFeedback` to tutorial gating paths may feel frustrating to tutorial players who are expected to make certain mistakes. Mitigation: the feedback is brief (0.15s reduced-motion, 0.1s normal shake + short SFX) and the text instruction remains; it provides clarity, not punishment.
- Risk: catching all try/catch errors with illegal feedback could mask genuine bugs (e.g., null-reference exceptions). Mitigation: console.error is already logged; the FX is the user-facing layer only. If an error message starts with "Error:" (as all current handlers do), the text remains as the primary signal.
- Assumption: `playIllegalFeedback` is always available in the context (it's a module-local function in the same file). No new imports needed.
- Scope-creep guard: this item only covers Main Street. Other example games that may have the same pattern are recorded as linked follow-up items, not expanded into this one.

## Existing state

- `playIllegalFeedback()` in `MainStreetTurnController.ts:34-82` — wraps `shakeIllegalMove` with container-safe fallback, plays `COMMON_SFX_KEYS.ILLEGAL_MOVE` via `safePlaySound`, respects reduced-motion.
- Several handlers already use it correctly: `onPeekClick` (line ~1275), `onCommunityFavourClick` (line ~1331), insufficient-coins catch blocks in `onDragDropBusiness` (line ~830), `onSlotClick` (line ~1003, 1014), `onUpgradeCardClick` legality (line ~1514), `onStaffCardClick` legality (line ~1611).
- Other handlers have only `s.instructionText.setText()` with no FX.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — Add `playIllegalFeedback` calls to all rejection paths identified above.

## Related work

- **Add best practices for animations and sounds on player/AI actions (CG-0MSHFOSGV007W8UC)** — completed; established the mandatory rule that all player and AI actions using core engine helpers must be animated and audible.
- **Main Street Game Feel: animation, audio & VFX enhancement proposals (CG-0MSRGTAA9001F2ST)** — completed; broader game feel improvements for Main Street.

# Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street

## Problem Statement

Main Street is single-player only; the `MainStreetState`, `MainStreetEngine`, and PRD M3 were never designed for an opponent. Players asked for competitive play — racing an AI on the shared street grid — but the engine assumes single ownership of coins, hand, actions, street slots, and score. Adding competitive mode requires splitting those concerns while preserving single-player behaviour and the existing AI/hint/Monte Carlo stack.

## Users & User Stories

- **Player (competitive mode):** As a Main Street player, I want to play against an AI opponent on the same shared street so each turn I have a rival to race and react to.
- **Developer / QA:** As a developer, I want a head-to-head Monte Carlo harness for competitive mode so balance between player and AI can be measured across seeded runs.
- **Future AI iteration:** As an AI developer, I want the AI decision layer ownership-aware and staff-free so competitive strategy is coherent without rewriting the hint/balance harness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Per-player state & ownership:** A competitive state model exists with per-player coins/reputation, hand, staff, action budget, and score, plus owner-tagged street slots; deterministic and replayable via seeded RNG. Single-player behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC2 — AI plays a legal competitive turn:** The AI generates legal actions through `enumerateLegalActions` (competitive mode) with staff actions excluded, scored by an ownership-aware `scoreAction`/helpers, and executed via `executeAction`. Verified with legality and determinism tests.
- [ ] **AC3 — Per-owner income; shared events:** Income accrues only to the owning player of each placed business; street-wide investment events and incidents retain their existing resolution semantics, routed per-owner as specified. Validated by income/event unit tests.
- [ ] **AC4 — Competitive Monte Carlo harness:** A head-to-head harness (extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) runs >=200 seeds and produces win/score distributions plus per-player metrics; single-player AI tests still pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Engine-only scope confirmed:** PRD M3 is updated to note this deliberate scope extension; competitive mode has no game-selector entry or scene yet — rendering (owner-coloured street, shared-market phase alternation with SFX/animations per AGENTS.md 8) is deferred to a planning-created child.
- [ ] **AC6 — Tests & docs:** Relevant unit tests and new tests cover AC1–AC4; build succeeds; affected docs/comments are updated.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full test suite passes** with the new changes (release gate; not a per-push requirement beyond `npm run build` + unit tests).

## Constraints

- Competitive mode scope is **state + engine + AI + Monte Carlo only** — no game selector entry, no competitive scene, no competitive UI chrome yet (AC5 deferred to a planning child).
- Turn alternation: **alternate MarketPhases within a shared day** (confirmed producer decision). Income/Incident/EndCheck phases are shared once both players have acted. Implementation design stays within planning.
- Win condition: **first player to reach the win threshold wins**; the game offers an endless continuation option beyond threshold (confirmed producer decision). Endless mode wiring is within the parent unless planning creates a dedicated child.
- `MainStreetAiPlayer` / `MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `enumerateLegalActions` are unchanged for single-player consumers.
- Determinism via seeded RNG is preserved; replays remain reproducible.

## Existing State

- Single-player-only state (`MainStreetState` resourceBank/hand/staffCards/actionsRemaining), engine (`applyIncome`, `resolveEvent`, `resolveIncident`, `computeScore`, `checkEndConditions`), PRD M3, and AI layers (`MainStreetAiStrategy`, `GreedyStrategy`, `scoreAction`, `MainStreetAiPlayer`, `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) built for one owner. Reusability findings documented in the original description.
- One child item already exists: **CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (ownership-aware, staff-free)**.

## Desired Change

Ship an **engine-level competitive mode**: per-player state + owner-tagged grid, per-owner income routing, shared event semantics, ownership-aware and staff-free AI scoring, and a competitive Monte Carlo harness — without changing single-player behaviour or adding competitive rendering. Record the scope extension in PRD M3 and plan the rendering/scene child for the next milestone.

## Decisions Since Original Item

- **Turn structure:** Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) confirmed by producer.
- **AC5:** Deferred to planning — will become a child for rendering/selector/scene work.
- **Denial reasoning:** Opponent-aware denial (blocking best slot, buying to deny) intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.
- **Win condition:** First to threshold wins, with an endless continuation option beyond threshold.
- **Owner-coloured street (AC5):** Means tinting each placed business's street slot by owner (e.g., player = blue, AI = red) so the shared grid's ownership is visually unambiguous.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Split to per-player resources/hand/staff/actions/score; owner-tagged `StreetGrid` slots.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Per-owner income, shared event/incident routing, shared-day phase handling, competitive helpers.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Ownership-aware `scoreAction`/per-type helpers + competitive `enumerateLegalActions` variant (staff excluded); single-player paths unchanged.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Competitive head-to-head harness (extension).
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` — Note competitive mode as deliberate scope extension beyond M3.
- `tests/main-street/*.test.ts` (+ new competitive tests) — Unit + deterministic replay coverage for AC1–AC4; existing guardrails still passing.

## Related Work

- Related work items (from `find_related`): CG-0MM5ZGB8U02S0BFO — Main Street Scenario & Tutorial (completed) · CG-0MOXGGZXJ002X6H3 — [test-failure] MainStreetScene animation scheduling (completed) · CG-0MS9NXIEX00880UV — [test-failure] hud-layer-contract (completed)

- Child: CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (existing; align description with this parent's clarified ACs).
- Existing state/engine/AI/monte-carlo layers are the implementation basis (see Existing State above).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **State split regressions in single player:** score/income/event paths silently ignore per-player split. Mitigation: keep single-player API shim and run full single-player regression suite.
- **Income/event routing divergence:** per-owner bugs hard to diagnose. Mitigation: explicit per-owner unit fixtures + deterministic replay across seeds.
- **AI ownership semantics under-tested:** greedy heuristics mis-score denial/synergy when ownership added. Mitigation: head-to-head harness + baseline comparisons (AC4).
- **Phase alternation complexity:** alternating MarketPhases within one day adds state machine edge cases. Mitigation: diagram shared-day phases in planning and cover transitions with unit tests.
- **Scope creep toward rendering:** temptation to start the selector/scene early. Mitigation: AC5 is explicitly deferred; new rendering asks become planning-linked children.

## Open Questions

None — all open intake questions have been answered by the producer (see Comments). Remaining design detail (per-player state shape, phase machine, Monte Carlo metrics schema, endless-mode trigger) is within planning.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Alternating turn structure — Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) vs Option B (alternate full days)?" — Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "a" → resolved as **Option A** (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day). Recorded in `wl comment` (producer decisions comment).

# Refactor Pass — Comprehensive Whole-Codebase Code Smell Detection & Remediation (CG-0MTCOQIRQ00541EJ)

## Problem Statement

The codebase has grown to ~46K lines of TypeScript without a systematic whole-repo refactor scan since earlier smell items were closed. Undetected linter issues (unused imports/variables) and architectural smells (god classes, long functions, duplicate code, engine-move opportunities) accumulate silently and degrade maintainability. A structured per-subdirectory pass is needed to auto-fix mechanical issues and file remaining smells as tracked Worklog items, with engine-extraction candidates prioritized as high.

## Users

- **Engine maintainers** — need a clean, lint-free codebase and a prioritized backlog of engine-extraction opportunities so shared modules absorb common patterns rather than duplicating them per game.
- **Game developers** — need to know which patterns in their game scenes (e.g., Main Street, Sushi Go, Beleaguered Castle) are candidates for promotion into `src/` so they can reuse engine APIs.

### User Stories

- As an engine maintainer, I want all linter-detectable issues (unused imports/vars, formatting) auto-fixed across the repo so the codebase is green without manual churn.
- As an engine maintainer, I want every remaining architectural smell (god class, long method, duplicate code, feature envy, inappropriate intimacy, magic numbers, unused code) filed as a Worklog work item with a REFACTOR comment at the source so nothing is lost and work is trackable.
- As a game developer, I want code that could be moved into the engine (card-system, rule-engine, core-engine, ai, ui) flagged as high-priority items so extraction can be scheduled first.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Linter auto-fix complete** — every subdirectory (`src/core-engine`, `src/card-system`, `src/rule-engine`, `src/ai`, `src/ui`, `src/balance-cards`, each `example-games/*` game, `tests`) scanned with the refactor skill's linter auto-fix; mechanical fixes (unused imports/vars, blank-line/style) applied in-place and committed.
2. **Smells filed** — every non-auto-fixable smell detected by the hybrid linter+LLM scan is recorded as a child Worklog work item under this epic (one item per distinct smell/instance), with severity, description, and file location; REFACTOR comments injected at the source location to prevent duplicate filing.
3. **Engine-move items prioritized high** — any smell or duplication where logic could be promoted into `src/` engine modules is filed with `priority: high` and tagged to indicate the target engine module (e.g., `engine-move:ui`, `engine-move:rule-engine`).
4. **No duplication of prior smells** — previously closed smell items (CG-0MM1OP07Q16TUTHI god class, CG-0MM1OPFLF07WCFYP long functions, CG-0MM1OP94103E36SI unsafe casts, CG-0MM1OQ5U80HVOPKJ move validation, CG-0MM1OPSGM052NPUN magic numbers, CG-0MM1OQN4E153GJY3 SFX keys) are not re-filed unless the smell has regressed.
5. **Build and tests green** — after auto-fix, `npm run build` succeeds and the full project test suite passes (`npm test` on release; at minimum `npm test -- --project unit` before push per quality gates) with no regressions.

## Constraints

- **Per-subdirectory scanning required** — full-repo `npx eslint .` OOMs at ~46K LOC (verified 2026-08-31); each scan must target a single subdirectory to stay within Node heap limits.
- **Whole-codebase scope, not session-boundary** — the refactor skill's default session-boundary mode (git diff vs `dev`) only covers recently changed files; this epic explicitly requires scanning all source subdirectories regardless of git status.
- **Auto-fix + file, not just report** — linter issues are auto-fixed in-place; architectural smells are filed, not silently reported.
- **Stage lifecycle** — this item is an `epic`; children are created for each smell category/instance and tracked to closure before the epic advances to `in_review`.

## Existing State

- Repo is ~46K lines TypeScript; prior systematic smell items are all **completed** (Stage `done`): god class, long functions, unsafe type assertions, inconsistent move validation, magic numbers, SFX naming.
- No current `.refactor.json` config; no open code-smell work items remain.
- `npx eslint .` on the full repo aborts with `FATAL ERROR: Ineffective mark-compacts near heap limit` (verified 2026-08-31).
- The refactor skill (`~/.pi/agent/skills/refactor/scripts/refactor.py`) supports `--no-llm` (linter-only) and `--no-linter` (LLM-only) modes, `--dry-run`, and per-directory invocation via file args; session-boundary detection defaults to `dev` branch.
- Only 1 file differs from `dev` (`tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts`), so the default session-boundary scan found no smells — confirming the need for explicit whole-codebase invocation.

## Desired Change

- Run the refactor skill's linter auto-fix across each subdirectory sequentially, committing fixes.
- Run the hybrid linter+LLM smell detection across each subdirectory, filing each distinct smell as a child Worklog item under CG-0MTCOQIRQ00541EJ with REFACTOR comments at the source; engine-move candidates flagged `priority: high`.
- Dedup against closed smell items to avoid noise; verify with `npm run build` and `npm test` (full suite on release, unit minimum before push).

**Key Files:**
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — Orchestration script to invoke per-subdirectory (linter auto-fix + LLM detection modes)
- `src/core-engine/**/*` — Engine module to scan; source of engine-move targets
- `src/ui/**/*` — Engine module to scan (largest UI surface, likely extraction source)
- `src/card-system/**/*`, `src/rule-engine/**/*`, `src/ai/**/*`, `src/balance-cards/**/*` — Engine modules to scan
- `example-games/**/*` (golf, main-street, sushi-go, beleaguered-castle, lost-cities, coloretto, feudalism, blackjack, gym) — Game code most likely to contain engine-move candidates
- `.refactor.json` (if created) — Optional project config to tune linter/LLM smell types and severity mapping

## Related Work

- **Potentially related work items:** CG-0MM1OP07Q16TUTHI (God class — completed), CG-0MM1OPFLF07WCFYP (Long functions — completed), CG-0MM1OP94103E36SI (Unsafe type assertions — completed), CG-0MM1OQ5U80HVOPKJ (Inconsistent move validation — completed), CG-0MM1OPSGM052NPUN (Magic numbers — completed), CG-0MM1OQN4E153GJY3 (SFX key naming — completed), CG-0MSUUDMJZ005VYZP / CG-0MSXL2L0T009CA3I (Quality Improvement — Refactoring, completed)
- **Potentially related docs:** `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (dev workflow, testing, quality gates), `docs/dev/release-process.md` (dev→main promotion), `~/.pi/agent/skills/refactor/SKILL.md` (refactor skill contract), `eslint.config.cjs` / `.eslintrc.cjs` (linter config), `AGENTS.md` (project conventions, Stage vs Status lifecycle)
- **Prior refactor pattern:** Earlier engine extractions (e.g., GymSceneUtils, deck grid, event log, SFX auto-discovery) demonstrate the spike-driven extraction workflow expected for high-priority engine-move items.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk: OOM on large subdirectories** — even a single large game directory (e.g., `example-games/main-street`) could approach heap limits; mitigation: split large games by file glob if needed and run with `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=4096` if required.
- **Risk: LLM false positives / noise** — LLM detection may flag non-issues; mitigation: operator triage on filed items; auto-close or deprioritize low-value findings.
- **Risk: Scope creep** — whole-codebase scan may surface many low-value smells; mitigation: file all but prioritize only engine-move candidates as high; others at author discretion per producer directive.
- **Risk: Auto-fix churn** — linter fixes may touch many files; mitigation: single commit per subdirectory or single commit for all auto-fixes, clearly titled, with build/test verification before push.
- **Assumption:** Producer intent is to file smells as children of this epic (not to fix all smells inline during the scan); fixing happens in the child items' own implement cycles.
- **Assumption:** `npm test -- --project unit` is the minimum gate before push; full suite (`npm test`) is release-only per AGENTS.md — epic's AC 5 reflects this.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Scope of 'entire codebase': do you mean (a) all TS files in the repo or (b) session-boundary only?" — Answer (producer @ 2026-08-31): "(a) entire codebase, not just recent changes. Look for smells and record them in the Worklog. Pay particular attention to code that could be moved into the engine (these items should be high priority - others at your discretion)" — Source: intake session comment thread on CG-0MTCOQIRQ00541EJ.
- Q: "Full-repo scan feasibility (OOM at ~46K LOC) — per-subdirectory or restrict to engine modules?" — Answer (producer): "per-subdirectory" — Source: same session.
- Q: "Fix vs. file: auto-fix linter errors in-place and file architectural smells, or just produce a report?" — Answer (producer): "auto-fix linter record smells in worklog" — Source: same session.
- Research summary: Verified OOM by running `npx eslint .` (heap OOM, mark-compact failure). Verified refactor skill dry-run in `--no-llm` mode against current session (1 file, 0 smells) — confirming default session-boundary mode is insufficient. Verified no `.refactor.json` exists. Searched `wl search refactor/smells/code smell` — 6 prior smell items found, all `completed`. Searched `grep -r REFACTOR` — no existing REFACTOR comments in the codebase. AGENTS.md and docs/DEVELOPER.md reviewed for quality gates and epic lifecycle.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MQK9N82B002Z6WJ** – Gym: Rule Engine demo scene (LegalityResult + EconomyLedger) (completed)
- **CG-0MPVPRZJA00147BH** – Create deck grid rendering utility (completed)
- **CG-0MT5XUE2200047IJ** – Main Street sold businesses still provide synergy (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: aborts, agent, agents, applied, approach (+287 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: aborts, acceptance, advances, agent, agents (+228 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-balance-process-and-tooling.md` — matched: agent, agents, answer, appendix, applied (+187 more)

# Add art notes to each card in CSV

## Problem statement

The Main Street card CSV (`example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`) lacks descriptive art notes for use with generative AI art tools. Each of the 154 cards needs a short, icon-focused description that captures what makes that card visually unique — the central icon that distinguishes it from all others.

## Users

- **Producer/Art Director**: Uses the notes as prompts when generating card artwork with tools like Midjourney, DALL-E, or Stable Diffusion.
- **Developer**: Reads notes to verify generated art matches the card's identity before integration.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A new column `art_notes` is added to `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv`.
2. Every card row (154 data rows) has a non-empty `art_notes` value.
3. Each art note describes **only the unique visual identifier/icon** for that card — no style, color, or layout information shared across cards.
4. Art notes are concise (one sentence, ~20–50 words), focusing on an identifiable object or symbol.
5. Notes are consistent within families: business cards describe the business icon, staff cards describe the person/object, event cards describe the scene element, upgrade cards describe the transformation icon, and community-space cards describe the landmark.

## Constraints

- CSV must remain valid and parseable — the new column must be placed at the end (after `peekOncePerTurn`).
- No style, color, or formatting descriptors (e.g. no "cartoon style," "dark background," "warm colors") — these are shared across all cards.
- Notes must be short enough to serve as effective AI art prompts.
- The `family` column determines the card category and helps ensure consistent note style within each family.

## Existing state

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` has 33 columns and 154 data rows (excluding header).
- Card families: business (30), staff (21), upgrade (39), event (56), community-space (8).
- Card SVGs already exist in `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/` with a consistent layout: dark background, colored header bar (by category), card name, cost circle, central icon area, and synergy category icon.
- The central icon area is the only per-card visual differentiator — this is what art notes should describe.

## Desired change

Add an `art_notes` column with descriptive text for each card. Examples of good art notes:

| Card | Art Note |
|------|----------|
| Bakery | A golden bread roll with a scored top, steam rising in three wavy lines. |
| Bookshop | An open hardcover book with visible text lines and a bookmark ribbon hanging from the page edge. |
| Arcade | A retro joystick with a red ball-top and two white buttons on a black base. |
| Accountant (staff) | A leather-bound ledger book with a gold calculator resting on top. |
| Block Party (event) | A string of triangular bunting flags stretched between two poles with musical notes floating above. |
| Upgrade to Restaurant | A chef's hat (toque) above crossed fork and knife, with steam rising between them. |

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — Source file to modify
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/` — Reference for existing card icons (optional)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **CSV compatibility**: Adding a column changes column count — any CSV consumers must be updated to handle the new column gracefully (ignore unknown trailing columns).
- **Art note quality variance**: Generative AI prompts benefit from consistent phrasing patterns; without a style guide, notes may vary in specificity.
- **Scope**: 154 cards is a large number of individual notes. Batch generation is expected.

## Related work

- CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ: Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- CG-0MM4RF91E1LR5RSY: Main Street: PRD Milestone 4 -- Visual Polish, Animation, and Audio (completed)

---

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

No questions asked — the work item description was sufficiently clear and the task is well-scoped.

# Core engine: charge an action for event move/play
Wire the event move/play paths into the existing Main Street action economy. Same-day composite mirrors the business-card model (move spends the action; same-day play of that just-moved event is free). Coins unchanged (no cost at move, `event.cost` at play).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `executeAction` cases `buy-event`, `play-event-from-hand`, and `play-event` call `consumeAction(state)` before delegating to `purchaseEvent`/`playEventFromHand`. Legality gating rejects event moves/plays when `actionsRemaining` is 0.
- [ ] `moveEventToHandCommand` and `playEventCommand` each call `consumeAction(state)` *inside* the snapshotted action body (undo-safe) and expose matching `canMoveEventToHand`/`canPlayEventFromHand` legality (action-budget gate).
- [ ] `canPurchaseEvent(state, ...)` rejects when hand capacity **or** `actionsRemaining ≤ 0`; `canPlayEvent(...)` (add if not already present) rejects under the same budget and additionally respects the same-day composite — playing the `justMovedHandCardId`-equivalent event on the same day does **not** double-charge.
- [ ] Same-day composite tracking: controller/engine reuse `justMovedHandCardId`-style semantics for events (set on move, checked on same-day play, cleared on end-turn/day reset). Playing a held event from a prior day costs 1 action; moving and playing the just-moved event costs 1 action total (no double charge).
- [ ] Controller/UI: `onEventCardClick` and `onPlayHeldEvent` gate on `actionsRemaining`, spend the single action for a composite via the command/engine path, and no longer claim events are free. Undo/redo reuses `UndoRedoManager` and invalidates the redo stack on new actions.
- [ ] `npm run build` and main-street unit tests pass; the one-child-per-task state regression coverage is unaffected.

Test fails before fix, passes after.

# Feature: Deterministic Banking AI Tests (BankingGreedyStrategy)

## Summary
Expand `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` to contract `BankingGreedyStrategy` (distinct class, not `GreedyStrategy`) for hoard/spend/cap/legality/difficulty; leave Greedy baseline untouched.

## Target Outcome
Deterministic, fast unit tests prove `BankingGreedyStrategy` deliberately hoards vs spends correctly and respects legality, before implementation lands.

## Definition of Done
- Suite imports `BankingGreedyStrategy` (name === 'BankingGreedy', implements MainStreetAiStrategy) alongside unchanged Greedy/Random.
- Cases: (a) hoards (end-turn with actionsRemaining>0) when an unaffordable high-value hand/market target exists, (b) spends when no valuable unaffordable target, (c) at bankedActions==2 returns spend (bank value 0), (d) respects enumerateLegalActions legality (no illegal action emitted), (e) difficulty scaling — Easy spends where Hard hoards on same state.
- Existing ai-action-budget + monte-carlo tests remain green (or drift documented).
- `npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` passes.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. New suite targets `BankingGreedyStrategy`; GreedyStrategy and RandomStrategy remain importable/unchanged.
2. Deterministic hoard vs spend vs cap vs legality cases covered (a–d above).
3. Difficulty scaling test: same state, Easy spends where Hard hoards (or quantified threshold difference documented).
4. No regression in existing ai-action-budget / monte-carlo tests (or documented drift).

## Minimal Implementation
- Retarget/create helper makeState({hand, market, coins, banked, difficulty/config}) in tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts.
- Table-driven tests for cases above; include helper to build MainStreetState with hand/market/business+upgrade/event cards and bankedActions.
- Run: `npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts`.

## Dependencies
None (test-first — blocks F2).

## Deliverables
- `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts` (expanded/retargeted)
- Passing unit run for touched file

## Key Files
- `tests/main-street/ai-banking-strategy.test.ts`
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts`
- `tests/main-street/ai-action-budget.test.ts`

## Constraints
- Main Street only; no core-engine changes.
- Do not modify GreedyStrategy behaviour in this slice — tests define the contract it must satisfy in F2.
